summary: This RFC registers an extension report type for the Abuse Reporting Format, for reports generated at receipt time about messages that fail email authentication checks.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 6591 adds a report type for email authentication failures. The report identifies the failed check and includes details that can help the sender investigate.

questions: what is an arf auth-failure report
subtitle: An ARF extension reports which email authentication check failed and why.

tldr.problem: A receiver may need to explain why an incoming message failed email authentication, including details that help the sender diagnose the failure.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6591 adds the auth-failure report type to ARF and defines required and optional fields for DKIM, ADSP, and SPF results.
tldr.outcome: A report describes one authentication failure and includes the original message headers. RFC 6591 is a Proposed Standard updated by RFC 6692 and RFC 9991.

today: RFC 6591 is a Proposed Standard published in April 2012. It has been updated by RFC 6692 and RFC 9991, and no RFC is listed as obsoleting it.

sections.title: Reporting an Authentication Failure
sections.content:
The Abuse Reporting Format (ARF) provides a structured message for reporting email abuse. RFC 6591 extends it to report messages that fail authentication checks such as DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) and Sender Policy Framework (SPF).

A report can include information about the specific reason the check failed. Each report describes one authentication failure; multiple reports may be sent for several failures in one message.
sections.plainLanguage: A receiving mail system can send an ARF report when a message fails an authentication check. The report gives the sender structured details about the failure.

sections.title: Required and Optional Report Fields
sections.content:
The new feedback type is auth-failure. Its machine-readable part must include Authentication-Results describing one authentication method's result and must include Auth-Failure. Reported-Domain is required when a value is available. The original message's full header block must be present as message/rfc822 or text/rfc822-headers.

Delivery-Result is optional and records the final handling, such as delivered, spam, policy, reject, or other. For a DKIM report, the domain, identity, and selector fields are required. An ADSP report requires DKIM-ADSP-DNS; an SPF report includes SPF-DNS for every record used.
sections.plainLanguage: The report must name the failure type and include authentication results. Depending on the check, it must also include the relevant domain, signature, selector, or DNS record details.

sections.title: Five Authentication Failure Types
sections.content:
Auth-Failure has five defined values. adsp means the message did not follow the domain's published signing practices. bodyhash means the signed body hash did not match. revoked means the signing key was revoked. signature means the DKIM signature did not verify. spf means the SPF evaluation returned none, fail, softfail, temperror, or permerror.

Some values require extra report fields. For example, revoked requires DKIM-Domain and DKIM-Selector. bodyhash recommends the canonicalized body, unless it would include data that was redacted.
sections.plainLanguage: The report names one of five failure types, such as a changed message body or a revoked key. Each type determines which extra details the report needs.

sections.title: Registering the New Report Vocabulary
sections.content:
The RFC adds auth-failure to the ARF feedback-type registry and registers ten new report fields. The fields include Auth-Failure, Delivery-Result, DKIM data, and SPF-DNS. Each is associated with the auth-failure report type and is registered as current.

The RFC also defines the syntax of the new fields using ABNF. For example, Auth-Failure accepts only the five defined values, and SPF-DNS records the type, domain, and retrieved record content.
sections.plainLanguage: The new report type and field names are added to ARF's registries. Their syntax is defined so systems can recognize the same values.

sections.title: Forgery, Report Floods, and Privacy
sections.content:
Authentication failure reports can be forged like ordinary email. A forged report could falsely claim that a message failed or provide fake signature details. The RFC suggests establishing reporting relationships in advance and taking care before automating actions based on reports.

Automatic generation can flood a recipient, including when an attacker sends messages designed to trigger reports. Rate limits or periodic summaries can reduce volume but may omit incident detail. Canonicalized DKIM data can help diagnose a failure, but may reveal private information, so including it is not required.
sections.plainLanguage: A report may be forged, and automatic reports may overwhelm a recipient. Agree with reporting partners in advance and consider privacy before including message data.

items.title: adsp
items.text: The message did not follow the domain's signing practices.

items.title: bodyhash
items.text: The body hash in the signature did not match.

items.title: signature
items.text: The DKIM signature did not verify.

items.title: spf
items.text: The SPF evaluation produced a reportable result.
